bet.text: A quick high and low goal cycle robot with a traversal climber.

auto.text: The spec sheet lists one to five ball autos, with paths from the team's own PathGen tool and constant acceleration interpolation.
Another team's pit scouting lists five upper hub shots.

cycle.text: In an off-season interview: the wide intake grabs cargo it touches, two beam breaks place two balls in the magazine, the Limelight gives target and distance, and the hood adjusts. Preferred spot: behind the tarmac. For cargo behind the hub the driver switches to a rear camera and robot-centric driving.

endgame.text: From the second bar, a one-stage elevator goes up, out to the next bar and pulls the robot onto fixed spring hooks, then repeats. The spec sheet gives 10 seconds to traversal; an off-season interview gives about 12 to 13 from the ground.

fallback.text: It can climb alone to any of the four bars and shoot into either hub.

changed.text: Many climbers came before the final one; a new one came out at the Colorado Regional. The backspin roller came before the first regional, because balls bounced out. An off-season interview describes a second, shorter feeder. In it, early tries stalled and swung on bar three, so the NavX accounts for the swing.

outcome.text: 52-18-0 in official play; finalist in the Hopper division; ranked 19 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 56.85, Hopper).

facts.text: SDS MK4 L2 modules, eight Falcons, with custom protectors
Speed
The team's first competition swerve chassis

solves.text: Keep any cargo the robot touches, also behind the hub where it is hard to see

facts.text: Four-bar linkage with vectored wheels
In an off-season interview: flexible polycarbonate, and the linkage collapses against walls
In that interview: pneumatics keep the front area clear of motors

cost.text: Spare intakes are kept ready in case one snaps (off-season interview)

functions.name: Feeder
functions.type: compliant wheel magazine for two balls

solves.text: Store two balls at consistent positions without wasting height

facts.text: In an off-season interview: compliant wheels keep every ball in contact
In that interview: beam breaks at the start of the magazine and just before the flywheel show where the balls are
Two balls reach the shooter in under
That interview describes a second version, shorter, about 12 in instead of about 14
In that interview a bump in the middle gives compression on both sides; it comes from a dual intake idea that was not finished

functions.name: Shooter
functions.type: central flywheel with adjustable hood and backspin roller

solves.text: Keep balls in the hub from many distances

facts.text: Flywheel on two Falcons
In an off-season interview: shoots from practically against the hub to the outer bounds of the field
Two balls in
The backspin compensation roller was critical to keeping balls in the hub; early tests bounced right out

functions.name: Limelight and driver camera
functions.type: vision targeting and rear camera driving

solves.text: Clear the two or three balls behind the hub that slow the robot down

facts.text: In an off-season interview: a Limelight on the front gives the target and its distance
A rear camera shows cargo behind the hub; one button changes field-centric driving to robot-centric, so the driver moves toward what it shows
The team says it used this a lot at the championship in Houston

functions.name: Climber
functions.type: one-stage elevator with a rotating arm and fixed spring hooks

solves.text: Reach the traversal bar while the robot swings between bars

facts.text: Two Falcons and a NEO 550
Spring-loaded hooks hold the bar below while the arm reaches the next
In an off-season interview the NavX compensates for the swing, so the hook meets the bar whichever way the robot tilts
Pit scouting at the championship lists about 15 seconds

cost.text: Asked whether NavX control was critical, a reply that reads as the team's says yes: the timing of the transitions was missed every time, mostly from bar 3 to bar 4

facts.text: Weight
Height
Pit scouting at the championship lists 29 by 29 in and 122 lb

decisions.choice: One-stage elevator with an articulating arm (off-season interview)
decisions.because: it is a lot more compact and the usual arrangement would not fit
decisions.instead_of: telescoping hooks plus a second set that leans the robot back

decisions.because: balls bounced right out in early testing

decisions.choice: A shorter feeder with a center bump (off-season interview)
decisions.because: it saves height and lowers the center of gravity
decisions.instead_of: one wheel with a curve on the back, which was tall

decisions.choice: Robot-centric driving with a rear camera
decisions.because: it clears balls behind the hub that are hard to see

decisions.choice: NavX control of the climber arm (off-season interview)
decisions.because: early tries left the robot stalling and swinging on bar three
